stem:
Soham folds the square sheet in the figure once down the middle, punches one hole through both layers, then unfolds the sheet.

Which claim correctly predicts the unfolded design?

options.text: The fold line itself is the punched design.
One hole appears anywhere on the paper, even where the layers did not meet.
Two holes appear as mirror images across the fold line, because the fold forced matching positions to coincide.
The punched holes are what create the fold line.

teacher.key_rationale: A single punch through both layers of a fold yields a mirror pair across the fold line. Naming the fold line swaps the design. Ignoring coincidence drops the symmetry condition. Punches do not create the fold.
teacher.figure_note: Square sheet with dashed midline fold and one punch mark on the left half.

mx_swap.reason: Scope-error CWO demands group-theory language not sayable with fold-and-punch objects; kept term_substitution, condition_omission, relationship_reversal.
